title: Threat model frontmatter
description: Frontmatter for a threat model under docs/security/. The one type that requires `reviewed`, because staleness is its whole failure mode and nothing else detects it, and the only one with a nested vocabulary: each finding carries one treatment, a response state, and the date that state last changed.

id.description: Stable document identifier. It does not change when the title or filename does.

type.description: Document category, from the standard's closed set.

status.description: Lifecycle state, from this type's controlled vocabulary. Agents do not invent statuses.

updated.description: Optional. Git already knows when the file changed; set this only where the document's own sense of currency differs from its last commit.

reviewed.description: When the analysis was last checked against reality. Required on this type alone. The cadence is a trigger rather than an interval, declared in docs/security/README.md.

owners.description: Who is answerable for the content. The first entry is the one answerable.

related.description: Declared relationships. Optional, so an absent relation proves nothing.

depends_on.description: Documents this one depends on. A separate field from `related`, not a relation within it.

supersedes.description: The record this one replaces. Reciprocated by that record's `superseded_by`.

superseded_by.description: The record that replaced this one. Reciprocated by that record's `supersedes`.

url.description: Canonical location, for a document that gets copied out of the repository.

revision.description: What the analysis was performed against. Provenance rather than an expiry: it says which structure was analysed, so a reader can tell whether the thing in front of them is the thing that was modelled. One 40-character SHA where the model covers one repository, or a map from repository name to SHA where it spans several, which is what a cross-repository model needs because no single commit dates its claims.

findings.description: Optional machine-readable findings. The findings themselves live in the body, which is the single source of truth; this list exists for a model that also wants them queryable, and every entry in it is validated against the same finding definition.

identifier.description: A document identifier such as SPEC-0012, ADR-0017 or ARCH-SECURITY.

target.description: A reference resolvable from outside this document: an identifier (SPEC-0004), a qualified identifier (lexicon:SPEC-0004), an issue or pull request (argus#142), or a repository-relative path to a document that has no identifier (docs/plans/2026-09-11-project-doc-template.md). A path target is never qualified with a repository prefix.

relatedEntry.description: One declared relationship, as a predicate and what it points at.

finding.description: One finding. `treatment` is the decision and `response_state` is progress; conflating them is why threat models rot. A treatment is not a document status and belongs to no status vocabulary.

id.description: A stable identifier, such as THREAT-0007.

treatment.description: The decision, exactly one per finding. `out-of-scope` is not here: it describes where the model's boundary is, not what was decided, so it belongs in the Scope section.

response_state.description: Progress, which applies to all four treatments because every one can be decided before it is done.

state_updated.description: When `response_state` last changed. This is the field that makes a finding which has been in-progress for eleven months visible as one.

target_date.description: Optional. When it is expected to reach `done`.

control.description: The control that reduces the risk. Required at `mitigated`.

evidence.description: That the control is in place: a test, a configuration, a code path, or a documented procedure. A control nobody can point at is not a control. Required at `mitigated`.

removed.description: What was removed or declined. Required at `avoided`, which is the only treatment that ends with less system.

recorded_in.description: Where the removal is recorded. Required at `avoided`.

party.description: Whose control handles it. Required at `transferred`.

obligation.description: The contract or agreement that makes it their obligation. Required at `transferred`. Transfer does not remove the vulnerability.

risk_owner.description: Who carries the risk. Required at `accepted`, because without it acceptance means whoever wrote the model accepted it on the project's behalf.

residual_risk.description: What is still true after the acceptance. Required at `accepted`.

review_trigger.description: Time-driven or event-driven, and observable either way, so somebody can tell whether it has fired. Required at `accepted`.

disclosure.description: Optional, and never derived from `treatment`. Publication is its own decision: a control can be incomplete, misconfigured, or bypassable in a way the write-up reveals.

allOf.$comment: A mitigated finding owes the control and evidence that it is in place.
An avoided finding owes what was removed and where that is recorded.
A transferred finding owes the party and the obligation that makes it theirs.
An accepted finding owes a named owner, the residual risk, and a review trigger.

x-lexicon-transitions.$comment: Allowed next statuses, from the transitions the standard states for this type. Carried rather than enforced: a schema validates one document at one moment and cannot see a prior status.
